PHASES has detected no astrometric companions, with masses down to 2.5 times that of Jupiter, in 37 binaries, with orbital periods from 0.1 to 100 yr, and semimajor axis separations from 0.2 to 5 AU.
we have found no evidence for astrometric companions down to the masses of giant planets in the 37 binaries we have observed.
we have used the astrometric observations of 37 binary systems to exclude the existence of astrometric companions as massive as giant planets in 8 of these binaries.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, for a given system, a limit to the presence of a companion can be set only in the region of the mass-period plane where a perturbed orbit is consistent with the observations and where the companion is not too far from the star.
, in the absence of a direct detection, a negative result in the form of a mass limit is more useful than a positive detection.

the limits to the mass-period phase space for astrometric companions are not as stringent as those derived from the analysis of radial velocity data for these systems, and the astrometric data are not competitive with radial velocities for the detection of low-mass companions.
